I have seen malware add a Windows System password, on windows XP, vista, 7, which is an encryption of the registry and it asks for a password -- I don't know if this has been extended upwards in OS. In this case the password is usually set to something trivial like: 123, 12345, 123456, m, or password.

Another thing to try, assuming OS is not tainted (other then being Windows itself), shut down Windows. Reboot system and when it's about half way booting (in the middle of the spiral loading logo) force-power-off your system. Give it 20 seconds, then power on your system, Windows should detect an improper startup and you should see an option to go into Windows recovery mode -- or select startup (I don't remember what's it's called exactly). The point is you can select System Restore. From System Restore pick an restore point that is about 1-2 weeks old; basiclly pick the restore point that is two or three points back, but not so far back you have major changes -- acceptable losses. Hopefully that brings you backwards, allows you access into your box. From there run a MalwareBytes scan, and re-scan for viruses. Then Re-run Windows updates to get back to current. Theoretically, you should be good to go at this point.
